acceptance_evidence: Actual source/schema review supports eight specific assisted workflows, not automatic directory-policy enforcement. Minimal role-assignment and supported managed-identity configuration is usable partial context; source-specific grouped interviews compile only explicitly attributed separate bound decisions. Both B03.02 GUIDs remain distinct.
supported_modes: Explicit AzureRM 4.50.0 raw Terraform with supplied local snapshots and optional plan; reviewed ARM roleAssignments 2022-04-01 and storage 2023-05-01/ExpressRoute port 2024-05-01 with existing no-restore Bicep; saved normalized evidence and injected scoped management-plane details. No directory/Graph/sign-in-log read, membership expansion, policy evaluation or authentication action.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit assignment principal type/role-definition identity and scoped resource context supporting an approved operating-model interview, not effective authorization.
evidence_requirements: Map complete direct/inherited management-group/subscription/resource grants, deny assignments, conditions and data actions to the approved operating model; supplied assignment subsets are not effective access.
Bind accountable central/workload responsibilities, approved role definitions and least-privilege scope to a redacted operating-model record with original-time evidence.
Reviewer decision: are actual grants aligned with that model, including exceptions, inherited/additive access, review/expiry and scope completeness?
recommendations.limitations: Principal-type/role-definition configuration is not membership, evaluated permissions, inheritance or approved organizational responsibility. No directory/principal/role-definition expansion or permission change occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit identity type and validated supplied user-assigned binding count on supported storage/Direct-port resources, plus a workload-authentication interview.
evidence_requirements: Distinguish attached system/user-assigned identity configuration from actual application credential selection, downstream authorization and supported workload coverage.

Reconcile the intended workload population and attributable redacted authentication evidence. Managed identities are special service principals, so the mere existence of a service principal is not a failure.
Reviewer decision: do supported workloads actually use approved managed identities instead of managed application secrets, with lifecycle/authorization and unsupported cases documented?
recommendations.limitations: Identity type/count is partial configuration only. No principal/tenant ID, user-assigned identity ID, credential, token, service-principal inventory or sign-in-log read is retained or performed. This GUID is distinct from the MSA account-provenance B03.02.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Specific account-authentication-provenance interview with explicit population, emergency exceptions and separate canonical-GUID decision.
evidence_requirements: Use an attributable redacted record to identify the actual authentication origin of accounts with Azure administrative rights, including guests/external identities and inherited access.
Do not infer work/school identity from email suffix, display name, directory userType=Member or a role assignment. Reconcile explicit emergency-access and approved external-account exceptions.
Reviewer decision: does the complete applicable account population use the approved work/school authentication origin, with individually documented exceptions and finite review validity?
recommendations.limitations: No Azure resource flag can authenticate account origin. This remains a specific human-evidence workflow; no directory user records, account names, Graph lookup, login or identity conversion occurs. It never aliases the managed-identity B03.02 GUID.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit role-assignment principal type with group-authority/membership interview, not effective transitive group permissions.
evidence_requirements: Reconcile complete group-based Azure assignments, actual transitive membership and exceptions to direct grants; Group principal type alone is insufficient.
Verify authoritative on-premises/cloud group management, synchronization/nesting constraints and role-assignable group requirements without assuming every nested or dynamic group is supported.
Reviewer decision: do approved groups and their managed memberships deliver the intended access, with ownership, periodic review and source-of-authority documented?
recommendations.limitations: No group creation, membership expansion, synchronization, directory role assignment or effective-permission computation occurs. User/principal names, IDs and condition text are withheld.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Specific Conditional Access coverage/enforcement interview with explicit included/excluded populations, enabled versus report-only state and evaluation evidence.
evidence_requirements: Reconcile all applicable Azure users/roles/resources, policy conditions, included/excluded users/apps and emergency/service-account treatment against attributable original-time policy/evaluation records.
Distinguish enabled from report-only/disabled policies and actual grant/session logic; a policy's existence, one sign-in or a template does not establish universal enforcement.
Reviewer decision: is the intended Azure-access population actually governed by the approved Conditional Access controls, with coverage gaps and licensing/exception constraints explicit?
recommendations.limitations: No Graph/directory/sign-in-log request, What If/evaluation trigger, policy creation/change or authentication action occurs. This is a source-specific human-evidence workflow, not a policy-presence pass.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Specific MFA requirement/coverage interview separating method registration, actual enforcement, prior claims and explicit emergency exceptions.
evidence_requirements: Reconcile the complete Azure-access user population with the actual MFA requirement path, applicable authentication strength, exclusions/emergency procedures and original-time evaluation evidence.
Distinguish a registered method or isolated challenge from enforced MFA, and understand prior/satisfied authentication claims rather than assuming every compliant session prompts again.
Reviewer decision: is MFA enforced for the approved applicable population with attributable coverage, finite validity and explicitly reviewed gaps/exceptions?
recommendations.limitations: No user registration inventory, authentication method, biometric, phone, credential, sign-in record or challenge is collected or modified. A tenant default or self-reported registration cannot automatically pass this control.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Scoped role-assignment context and explicit central/workload responsibility interview, not inferred accepted delegation.
evidence_requirements: Document accountable central/platform and workload responsibilities for security, access, resource changes, operations, incident escalation and review using an accepted responsibility matrix.
Reconcile actual delegated scopes and least-privilege grants with those responsibilities, inherited/deny/conditional access and managed exceptions.
Reviewer decision: have responsible humans explicitly accepted and operationalized the centralized/delegated model for the applicable landing-zone population?
recommendations.limitations: An assignment scope is not organizational agreement, readiness or operational ownership. No RBAC change, directory enumeration, owner impersonation or fabricated acceptance is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Specific PIM eligibility/active/permanent-access interview with time bounds, approvals, activation evidence and emergency exception reconciliation.
evidence_requirements: Reconcile actual eligible, activated, permanent-active and time-bound assignments separately for Azure resource roles, Entra roles and relevant groups, including inherited access.

Verify least-privilege definitions, maximum activation duration, approval/MFA/justification, review/audit and attributable activation evidence; PIM presence does not establish zero standing privilege.

Reviewer decision: is standing privilege removed where intended, with explicitly justified emergency-access exceptions and accountable finite review rather than silently treating emergency permanent roles as compliant?
recommendations.limitations: No PIM grant/activation, Graph/directory/audit request, role change or privileged action is performed. Configuration or eligibility alone is not activation enforcement, and directory roles do not imply Azure-resource access.
